userStories.title: Add readMetaLoop config reader (off default | observe, fail-safe)
userStories.description: As a cam operator, I need a project-scoped [loop] meta_loop config value so the inter-cycle drainer can be turned on (observe) or left off, with any unknown value resolving to off (fail-closed) so the loop is never armed by a typo.
acceptanceCriteria: A new exported reader (e.g. readMetaLoop(configPath?)) reads [loop] meta_loop from scripts/cam/project.toml and returns the literal 'observe' only when the value is exactly the string 'observe'; it returns 'off' for an absent file, absent [loop] section, absent key, non-string value, malformed TOML, or ANY other string value (e.g. 'auto', 'on', 'observ'). [oracle: bun test -- test/config/meta-loop.test.ts (cases: absent file, [loop] absent, key absent, value 'off', value 'observe', value 'auto', value 'OBSERVE')]

A MetaLoop type (e.g. type MetaLoop = 'off' | 'observe') is exported and the reader's return type is MetaLoop. The reader mirrors the readMergeMode/readPlanApproval shape in the same file (try/loadConfig/section-guard/catch-default, configPath override defaulting to process.cwd()-relative project.toml). [oracle: grep -q "export function readMetaLoop" src/config/models.ts]

The unknown-value case asserts 'off' specifically (NOT just non-'observe'): the test feeds a fixture with meta_loop = 'auto' and asserts the result === 'off', so a future regression that returns 'auto' verbatim fails. [oracle: bun test -- test/config/meta-loop.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
bun run check:all passes green (typecheck + test + embed-vendor + ratchets + biome + ci-parity). [oracle: named-command `bun run check:all`]
userStories.notes: File: src/config/models.ts (add readMetaLoop + MetaLoop type next to readMergeMode @ ~144, readPlanApproval @ ~221). Test: test/config/meta-loop.test.ts (mirror test/config for readMergeMode/readPlanApproval; write tmp fixture project.toml under a tmp dir, pass as configPath). Gotcha: meta_loop is PROJECT-scoped (scripts/cam/project.toml [loop]); do NOT consult per-user config or CAM_CONFIG_PATH (CAM-53; see file header comment lines 4-6). Fail-closed posture: unknown -> off, never observe (CAM-96). Spec AC#1. Read scripts/cam/patterns.md at story start for on-main/config invariants.

userStories.title: Add 'meta-loop-observe' WorkerEventKind and detail type
userStories.description: As an operator replaying the event log, I need a structured kind:'meta-loop-observe' event with a well-typed detail so I can see what the drainer would select (or that the queue drained) without reading source.
acceptanceCriteria: 'meta-loop-observe' is added to the WorkerEventKind union in src/supervisor/events.ts. [oracle: grep -q "'meta-loop-observe'" src/supervisor/events.ts]

A detail interface/type (e.g. MetaLoopObserveEventDetail) is exported as a discriminated union of exactly two shapes: { wouldSelect: string; rank: number; wsjf: number } (a plannable issue would be picked) OR { drained: true } (queue empty). It is added to the WorkerEventDetail union so a WorkerEvent with kind:'meta-loop-observe' typechecks with this detail. [oracle: grep -q "MetaLoopObserveEventDetail" src/supervisor/events.ts]

A unit test constructs both detail variants and asserts they are assignable to WorkerEventDetail and round-trip through JSON.stringify with the expected keys ({wouldSelect,rank,wsjf} and {drained:true}). [oracle: bun test -- test/supervisor/meta-loop-event.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
bun run check:all passes green (typecheck + test + embed-vendor + ratchets + biome + ci-parity). [oracle: named-command `bun run check:all`]
userStories.notes: File: src/supervisor/events.ts (add kind to WorkerEventKind union @ ~59-81; add MetaLoopObserveEventDetail interface near the other *EventDetail types ~225-249; add it to the WorkerEventDetail union @ ~252-265). Test: test/supervisor/meta-loop-event.test.ts. The detail SHAPE is fixed by spec AC#3: {wouldSelect,rank,wsjf} | {drained:true}. wsjf is a SCALAR number here (the computed WSJF), not the WsjfScore object. Emitted to the supervisor-owned log .claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl (do not invent a new channel; spec gotcha). Spec AC#3.

userStories.title: Pure injectable observe decide-fn with dedup + drained detection
userStories.description: As the meta-loop, I need a pure, unit-testable function that, given the backlog selector and the last-emitted selection, returns the meta-loop-observe event to emit (or none), encapsulating selection-change dedup and drained detection, so all the observe decision logic is testable without any sidecar I/O.
acceptanceCriteria: A new module (e.g. src/supervisor/observe.ts) exports a pure decide-fn that takes the result of selectPlannableIssue (an IssueEntry or null) plus the last-emitted selection state and returns either a MetaLoopObserveEventDetail to emit (with the updated state) or a signal that nothing should be emitted. No filesystem/network/git I/O lives in this function; the selector is passed in (injected), not called internally. [oracle: grep -q "export function" src/supervisor/observe.ts]

When the selector returns a plannable IssueEntry, the returned detail is { wouldSelect: <issue.id>, rank: <issue.rank ?? a defined fallback>, wsjf: <computed WSJF scalar for that issue> }. [oracle: bun test -- test/supervisor/observe.test.ts]
When the selector returns null, the returned detail is { drained: true }. [oracle: bun test -- test/supervisor/observe.test.ts]

Dedup: feeding N consecutive ticks with the SAME selected id yields exactly ONE emit (first tick emits, subsequent ticks with unchanged selection emit nothing); the test runs >= 3 identical ticks and asserts exactly one emit. [oracle: bun test -- test/supervisor/observe.test.ts]

Re-emit on change: a tick whose wouldSelect differs from the last-emitted id emits again; a transition from a plannable id to null emits the {drained:true} event exactly once, and staying drained across further ticks emits nothing. [oracle: bun test -- test/supervisor/observe.test.ts]
The new test(s) fail when run against the pre-implementation source (HEAD) and pass after the change, proving they exercise new behavior, not a tautology. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
bun run check:all passes green (typecheck + test + embed-vendor + ratchets + biome + ci-parity). [oracle: named-command `bun run check:all`]
userStories.notes: New file: src/supervisor/observe.ts. Test: test/supervisor/observe.test.ts. Selector contract: src/issues/select.ts selectPlannableIssue(backlog: IssueEntry[]) => IssueEntry | null (and selectPlannableFromFile(cwd, spawn) for the I/O seam, used by US-004). IssueEntry (src/issues/types.ts) carries id, rank?, wsjf?: WsjfScore. The wsjf SCALAR for the event is the `.wsjf` field of computeWsjf's return value (src/issues/rank.ts:49 returns { wsjf, warning }: take `.wsjf`, discard `.warning`); the formula is (value+timeCriticality+riskReduction)/jobSize with missing-wsjf / jobSize<=0 -> 0. computeWsjf is currently PRIVATE: either export it from rank.ts (surgical) and reuse, or replicate the formula with the same guard in observe.ts. Event detail stays {wouldSelect, rank, wsjf:number}. Do NOT couple this fn to the filesystem (keep selectPlannable injected). Dedup state is a plain value passed in/out, NOT a file (CAM-68; spec gotcha). Spec AC#3, AC#5, AC#8 (anti-tautology). Resist preparing any flip/dispatch here (CAM-139 owns that). Read patterns.md for noUncheckedIndexedAccess guards.

userStories.title: Wire observe drainer into the sidecar idle-tick (off byte-identical)
userStories.description: As the long-lived sidecar process, I need the observe drainer invoked on the idle tick only when meta_loop=observe, the loop is inactive (active!==true), and no prd.json cycle is in flight, so the meta-loop observes between cycles and stays silent during an active or paused-mid-cycle run; when off it must be byte-identical to today.
acceptanceCriteria: RunSidecarLoopOptions gains an optional opts.runMetaLoopObserveFn?: () => void | Promise<void>, called inside the active!==true branch of runSidecarLoop (alongside opts.runMergeWatchFn) ONLY when a prd.json cycle is NOT in flight (the prd-in-flight check is in addition to active!==true: an active:false state with a present in-flight prd.json must NOT invoke the observe fn). [oracle: grep -q "runMetaLoopObserveFn" src/supervisor/loop.ts]

In src/commands/sidecar.ts (buildSidecarLoopDeps ~441-493) the production runMetaLoopObserveFn is produced via readMetaLoop: it is undefined (inert) when meta_loop==='off' and wired (calls the observe decide-fn over selectPlannableFromFile on the MAIN backlog + emits via logEvent) when meta_loop==='observe'. [oracle: grep -q "readMetaLoop" src/commands/sidecar.ts]

Off is byte-identical: an integration test runs runSidecarLoop with meta_loop off (runMetaLoopObserveFn absent) plus an injected selectPlannable spy, and asserts the spy is NEVER called and NO 'meta-loop-observe' event is emitted across multiple idle ticks. [oracle: bun test -- test/commands/sidecar-meta-loop.test.ts (assert selectPlannable spy call count === 0 AND zero meta-loop-observe events)]

Observe wouldSelect: an integration test with meta_loop=observe, active:false, no in-flight prd.json, and a backlog fixture containing a plannable issue asserts exactly one 'meta-loop-observe' event with detail {wouldSelect,rank,wsjf} matching the fixture's top-ranked issue. [oracle: bun test -- test/commands/sidecar-meta-loop.test.ts]

Observe drained: an integration test with meta_loop=observe and an empty/all-blocked backlog fixture asserts exactly one 'meta-loop-observe' event with detail {drained:true}. [oracle: bun test -- test/commands/sidecar-meta-loop.test.ts]

No mutation: across the observe ticks the test asserts the injected flipActiveFn is NEVER called, NO prd.json is written (a write-prd spy / file-mtime assertion shows zero writes), and the backlog fixture file is unchanged. [oracle: bun test -- test/commands/sidecar-meta-loop.test.ts (assert flipActive spy call count === 0 AND prd write spy count === 0)]

Quiet during active/paused-mid-cycle: an integration test asserts that when active:true, OR when active:false but an in-flight prd.json is present, runMetaLoopObserveFn is NOT invoked (no observe event emitted). [oracle: bun test -- test/commands/sidecar-meta-loop.test.ts]

Dedup state lives in-memory in the sidecar process (a closure/local in buildSidecarLoopDeps or the produced fn), NOT persisted to any file under .claude or the working tree. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
The new test(s) fail when run against the pre-implementation source (HEAD) and pass after the change, proving they exercise new behavior, not a tautology. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

userStories.title: Notify-on-drain via a drain-specific Resend message (reuse client, not the escalateFn)
userStories.description: As an operator, I want a Resend notification when the queue drains (and only then) so I'm pinged when there's nothing left to plan; it must carry a drain-specific message, NOT the alarming max-rounds non-convergence message, and must reuse the existing Resend primitives rather than instantiate a second client.
acceptanceCriteria: A NEW drain-specific notification fn is built that reuses readResendConfig + sendEscalation with a drain subject/body (e.g. subject "[cam] Backlog drained: no plannable issues remain"); it is explicitly NOT the existing non-convergence escalateFn closure (subject "[cam] Non-convergence: max review rounds reached"). No second Resend client is instantiated. [oracle: grep -q "drained" src/commands/sidecar.ts (drain-specific notify fn present) AND reviewer-judgment that sendEscalation/readResendConfig are reused, not re-implemented]

When the observe drainer emits a {drained:true} event AND Resend is configured (readResendConfig returns non-empty apiKey AND non-empty recipient), the drain notification is sent exactly once for that drain transition. [oracle: bun test -- test/commands/sidecar-meta-loop.test.ts (sendEscalation spy: call count === 1 on the drain emit)]

The drain email carries the DRAIN subject/body, not the non-convergence message: the test asserts the sendEscalation call's subject matches the drain message and does NOT contain "Non-convergence". [oracle: bun test -- test/commands/sidecar-meta-loop.test.ts (assert call arg subject includes the drain text AND not /Non-convergence/)]

When Resend is NOT configured (apiKey or recipient empty) the drain still emits its {drained:true} event but NO notification is sent: sendEscalation is never invoked. [oracle: bun test -- test/commands/sidecar-meta-loop.test.ts (sendEscalation spy call count === 0 with empty config)]

Dedup carries through: staying drained across further ticks does NOT re-fire the notification (sent once per drain transition, not per tick). [oracle: bun test -- test/commands/sidecar-meta-loop.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
bun run check:all passes green (typecheck + test + embed-vendor + ratchets + biome + ci-parity). [oracle: named-command `bun run check:all`]
userStories.notes: File: src/commands/sidecar.ts. F-03 CORRECTION: do NOT reuse the existing escalateFn closure @475-487 — it is hardcoded to the MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT subject "[cam] Non-convergence: max review rounds reached" and reusing it verbatim would send a semantically WRONG, alarming email on a mere drain. Instead build a NEW drain notify fn that reuses readResendConfig (@ src/config/models.ts:185) + sendEscalation (@ src/notify/resend.ts:70, EscalationOptions {apiKey, recipient, subject, html}) with a drain subject/body. The spec gotcha 'nao duplicar cliente Resend' forbids only a SECOND Resend client; reusing readResendConfig + sendEscalation with a drain message satisfies it. The drain notify fn is invoked by the US-004 runMetaLoopObserveFn when its emit is {drained:true} and resendConfig.apiKey!=='' && resendConfig.recipient!==''. Test: extend test/commands/sidecar-meta-loop.test.ts. Inject the sendEscalation seam (spy) + readResendConfig fixture (configured vs empty). The 'configured -> 1 call with drain subject / unconfigured -> 0 calls / subject is NOT Non-convergence' assertions are the NEGATIVE-assertion oracles the spec mandates (not a tautology). Spec AC#6.
